implementation_notes: The idiomatic Swift wrapper is a struct with a single stored property: value semantics plus synthesized Equatable/Hashable/Codable replace the hand-written wrapper, and RawRepresentable adds the raw-value conversion that Foundation's own identifier types (Notification.Name, NSUserInterfaceItemIdentifier) use. Make the initializer failable or throwing so validation happens at the one construction point; declaring any initializer in the type suppresses the memberwise one, so callers cannot skip the check.
pitfalls: An internal/public stored property plus the compiler's memberwise initializer lets any caller build an unchecked value; declare your own initializer (which suppresses it) and prefer a private member with a named accessor.
Codable synthesis encodes the stored property as a key, so the JSON becomes an object; a raw-value or custom Codable conformance is needed when the wire format must stay a bare scalar.
Conformances that erase the distinction - ExpressibleByStringLiteral, init(_:) from the raw type, or a free operator - re-admit raw literals everywhere and defeat the pattern.

variants.name: Tagged phantom-type wrapper
variants.implementation_notes: When a wrapper should carry no behaviour and one generic type should cover many tokens, the swift-tagged library supplies a phantom-type wrapper: Tagged<User, Int> and Tagged<Subscription, Int> are different types over the same representation, with rawValue access and the usual conformances provided. It removes the boilerplate of declaring a struct per identifier and is a good fit for ids in application code; the trade-off is a third-party dependency and less room for per-type behaviour, which then needs a typealias plus extension.
pitfalls: The tag exists only in the type system: Tagged<User, Int> and Int interconvert through rawValue/init, so boundary code must stay disciplined.
Conformances and validation live on the generic wrapper, so a per-id invariant still needs a dedicated typealias plus extension (or a real struct).
